api:
Setup: sys.path += [harness dir]; import harness as H.
Example call: res = H.ctl_run(cid, params, H.footprint('hollow3'|'ring4'|'disk4x4'), world, H.seeds(n, block), threads=6, latency='d0'|'dmin'|float, charge='relay'|'receptor'|'none', privileged=None, t_ref_min=0.5, quant=False, lib=None).
- world: a WORLDS name ('base1', 'base', 'pool', 'blink20', 'flash6', 'flip_mid', 'lead', 'decoy_lite', 'wound25', ...) or a WorldSpec.
- res is a build.Lives (so res['F'] works) plus res.diag [n,16] and res.latency.
Other calls:
- H.ctl_batch(cid, cand, fp, world, seeds): F matrix [n_cand, n_seeds], common random numbers.
- H.tissue_run(body, world, seeds): a tissue body on the same scratch kernel.
- H.best_reflex(world, seeds): the better of frozen and recorded re-tuned reflexes, on those lives.
- H.paired(a, b): mean ± SE of the per-life F difference.
- H.es_tune(...): separable CMA-ES.
- Parameter helpers: H.params, H.bayes_params(world), H.rnn_params.
Building your own controllers: python make_ckernel.py --fast --out DIR/x.so --ctl my.c; register in C with CTL_REGISTER, id >= 1000.
controllers: 0 null: never acts (used by the stream-equality test)
1 C0 central reflex (info-matched): a column's ping strokes that column's act cell; a centre ping taps; refractory periods. Calibration against reflex@hollow3

2 C1 privileged pursuit: reads the truth every dt, steers eventual dot position onto the extrapolated target, uses the true flip sign, taps when the predicted distance < 0.8 rho_c and the key will click, avoids poison, chases positive blob 1. use_dark=0 gives a 'perfect sensing + memory' variant
3 C2 generic tracker (info-matched, 15 params): pings in the efference frame, exponential forgetting, background-subtracted centroid, steer, tap on strong centred evidence, optional blind arc search
4 C3 tiny RNN (info-matched weights hook): fixed tick; inputs are ping counts per sense cell + key state + hotspot twitch; tanh recurrent layer; per-act-cell stroke outputs

5 C4 Bayes grid tracker (info-matched with world rules as params): posterior over target position (visible/dark mass) from ping likelihoods, no-ping evidence, diffusion, timer re-placement, blink, and its own commanded clicks; taps at posterior mass >= q_tap; steers to the best rho_c box
99 replay: replays a stroke schedule (exactness test)
latency_rule: A ping reaches the controller at its tissue delivery time c_j + d_min. Every commanded stroke happens at >= (time of the deciding callback) + latency; the harness enforces this, and a callback at t has seen only pings delivered at or before t. Per act cell there is also a minimum interval t_ref_min = 0.5 between strokes. Default latency = d0: the median one-hop vertical contact delay, dl = d0*exp(delay_sd*N)*(1±jit) + delta, floored at d_min, with delta = 0. That gives 1.0 in base1 and 0.5 at d0 0.5, so the full receptor-to-stroke chain is d_min + d0, like reflex@hollow3's median. The value is recorded per life in res.latency; 'dmin' or any number is also accepted.
validation: Determinism: C0, C1, C2 and C4 give identical ledgers with 6 vs 1 threads, fast vs full build, and full build run twice (hashes too). The scratch kernel's tissue path equals the repo kernel bitwise (ledger except the repurposed columns 21-22; spikes, fate, chem and world hashes) in base1 and pool.

Stream equality, null controller vs inert program body with the same footprint: 32/32 world x footprint cells (16 worlds x hollow3/ring4, 32 lives each) are bitwise equal on the world hash, rec_cand, rec_accept, respawns, samples, dist_sum, zone_samples, path, X/Y_end, kills and n_end. live_time differs only by summation order (relative difference <= 2e-14).

Replay: a tissue reflex@hollow3's act-plane raster, replayed through the controller path, reproduces the world hash, captures, misses, clicks, b2 clicks, nudges, path, dot end position, receptor columns, kills and income bitwise in 16/16 worlds (base, POOL, blink, flash, flip, lead, 4 b2 worlds, 2 wound worlds).

C0 vs tissue reflex@hollow3, 256 lives, block 1. base1: +0.03 ± 0.12 (8.77 vs 8.73). base d0 0.5: -0.07 ± 0.12 (9.35 vs 9.42). POOL: +0.11 ± 0.09 (4.78 vs 4.66). Captures and misses agree to 0.2 per life; costs differ by < 0.002 F.
Scoring setup: 256 fresh lives per world, block 2; diffs are vs the best reflex. Best reflex F: base 9.55, base1 8.77, POOL 5.09 (re-tuned), blink20 3.69 (re-tuned here), flip_mid 3.78, lead 2.20.
C3 RNN (292 weights, base1): F -1.13 at the random start, -0.65 after a short ES. The hook works but did not learn.
CPU-s per life (192 lives, 6 threads, loaded machine). null 0.011-0.019; C0 0.011-0.020; C1 0.016-0.024; C2 0.020-0.027; C4 0.13-0.25 (0.21 with the blink model); tissue reflex 0.027-0.037.
tests/test_harness.py: 19/19 pass in about 5 s (stream equality, replay, determinism, latency enforcement, info-matched controllers cannot read truth).
first_look: Best reflex F per world (256 fresh lives, block 2): base 9.55 (frozen), base1 8.77 (frozen), POOL 5.09 (re-tuned rt-nichemap), blink20 3.69 (re-tuned rt-harness), flip_mid 3.78 (frozen), lead 2.20 (frozen).

blink 20/20 (d0 1). C1 84.5 (+80.9). C1 use_dark=0 45.9 (+42.2). C2 tuned 5.7 (+2.0 ± 0.1). C4 tuned 9.1 (+5.4 ± 0.2). C4 makes 4.6 captures while the target is dark vs the reflex's 1.4. C4 without its blink model: +4.9.

flip midlife U[256,768] (d0 1). C1 84.5 (+80.8). C2 tuned 5.7 (+1.9 ± 0.2). C4 tuned 9.8 (+6.0 ± 0.2). The C2/C4 lead is entirely pre-flip: 0.1-0.3 captures after the flip, vs the reflex's 0.06 and C1's 89.
lead v_t 0.3, tau_turn 200 (d0 1). C1 76.0 (+73.7). C2 tuned 5.9 (+3.7 ± 0.1). C4 tuned 2.3 (+0.1 ± 0.1); its diffusion motion model fails on straight fast targets.
sec_per_life: CPU-seconds per life on the loaded 14-core machine: C0, C1, C2 and the null controller take 0.011-0.027; tissue reflex@hollow3 takes 0.027-0.037. C4 takes 0.13-0.25 (0.21 with the blink model), above the 0.2 s target in blink and lead. A 16 x 64-life ES generation of C2 takes about 3 s wall on 6 threads.
caveats: The sticks are lower bounds on what they measure. C1 is a heuristic pursuit, so the true ceiling is higher. C2 and C4 are approximate observers: 'no gain' does not prove the information is absent, while 'gain' does prove it is present.

C1's ceiling is dominated by knowing where the target is re-placed (+74 to +88 F). It mostly measures the value of omniscient target localisation, not any one capability. C1 ignores pings, so it scores the same in base1, blink20 and flip_mid, and in base and POOL (up to about 0.001 F of ping charge).

flip_mid is NOT yet an information test of switching. No shipped info-matched controller detects the flip, and their lead over the reflex is all pre-flip. Flip-detection controllers are for the capability agents.

C4 receives world rules (halo, rates, placement law, timer, blink rates) as parameters via bayes_params. These are fixed per world, never per-life hidden state, but they are an assumed world model. Its diffusion motion model fails in lead; a velocity-state filter is needed there.

Central computation is free (no cost for memory or long-range messages), and the fixed footprint pays no development cost. The measured gaps are therefore upper bounds on what a grown local tissue could gain. The prior study found grown bodies lose 1.8-3.2 F against program bodies.

kappa is continuous unless quant=True. Strokes are limited to one per act cell per 0.5; there is no limit on how many cells stroke at once. Ping charge 'relay' books one contact per ping; C0 vs reflex shows the net effect is < 0.002 F.

Own-action models (efference copy, twitch, key) assume an intact body and the assumed motor sign. With wounds, commands to dead cells are silently dropped and the models drift. Info-matched controllers are not told about deaths.

Tuned C2 and C4 tap very freely (40-73 misses per life): with c_miss 10 against R_cap 500, a tap pays at a 2% capture chance. The 'tuned' numbers come from light tuning (C2: 15 generations; C4: 8 generations, decision knobs only) on block 5, scored on block 2.

Best reflex: frozen reflex@hollow3 vs re-tuned sets from prior studies (nichemap, headroom v4/v5/v6) plus this harness's own re-tunes for blink20, flip_mid and lead (budget 100, blocks 7/8). The best is chosen on the scoring lives, which slightly favours the reflex. flip_mid's prior re-tunes were tuned on the flip family, not on all-midlife flips.

blink20, flip_mid and lead run at today's d0 1 (as in the prior study); the d0 0.5 variants (blink20f, flip_midf, leadf) are supported but were not scored. b2 and wound worlds were checked only by the stream/replay tests and quick C1 runs, not scored.
C3 (generic RNN) did not learn to catch in a 25-generation run; treat it as a hook.

Only the heap scheduler is supported in controller mode. The scratch ledger columns 21/22 mean dark / late captures on this kernel only. t_flip per life is drawn from the life seed with numpy, not with the prior study's flip_family.
